clue.text: Nitty-gritty of piles below underwear

indicators.note: below says the piles come under the underwear, i.e. after it in a down entry

parts.note: bras are items of women's underwear
piles and stacks are both heaps

explanation.surface: An earthy remark about what lies under someone's knickers, with a sly medical pun on piles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piles' wants to be the ailment; here it means heaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting down to the basic facts is an idiom for the nitty-gritty, the essential practical details.

clue.text: Ignorance of Bach's first violin playing

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of each of the words of and Bach's
playing suggests the violin's letters being worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: A musical remark: not knowing Bach's first violin piece, or a violinist playing it obliviously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bach's first' looks like his first work; 'first' instead takes the initials of 'of Bach's', and 'playing' is the anagram signal, not a performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Oblivion is a state of unawareness, a loose sense of being uninformed; some solvers felt this stretched.

clue.text: Academic abandons extravagant tie

indicators.note: abandons says the academic leaves the longer word

parts.note: profligate means wastefully extravagant
prof is short for professor, an academic

explanation.surface: A lecturer gives up wearing a flamboyant necktie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandons' removes PROF from the front of PROFLIGATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To ligate is a surgical verb meaning to bind or tie off, as with a blood vessel.

clue.text: Flog cash, reducing capital by 50%

indicators.note: the capital letter of cash is C, Roman 100; halving it gives L, Roman 50, so the first letter is swapped

explanation.surface: A finance instruction: sell off money while halving your capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flog' reads as sell, and 'capital' as money; it is the initial letter, C (100), halved to L (50).
explanation.definitionFit: To lash someone is to whip or beat them, the same as to flog.

clue.text: A poo gushes out from this part of the digestive system

definitions.text: this part of the digestive system

indicators.note: out signals the letters of the phrase coming out in disorder

explanation.surface: A scatological joke about something emerging from a body part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges A POO GUSHES; the joke is that the gullet is the wrong end for that.
explanation.definitionFit: The gullet, the tube carrying food from throat to stomach, is a part of the digestive tract.

clue.text: This man turned over region chasing ultimate in psychopathic monster

indicators.note: chasing puts the man and region after the psychopath's last letter
ultimate in picks the final letter of psychopathic

parts.note: this man, from the speaker's view, is him

indicators.note: turned over says the word for region is read backwards

parts.note: a region is an area

explanation.surface: A thriller picture: a man overturns a district in pursuit of a psychopathic beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned over' reverses the region word; 'chasing' means the man and region come after the last letter of 'psychopathic', not that anyone is pursued.
explanation.definitionFit: The chimaera of Greek myth was a fire-breathing beast, part lion, goat and serpent.

clue.text: Urge to break into the perimeter of Kashmir's national park

indicators.note: into says the reordered letters go inside the edge letters
the perimeter of takes just the edge letters of Kashmir
to break says the letters of urge are broken up and reordered

explanation.surface: A desire to cross the border of Kashmir and enter its wildlife reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to break into' reads as one phrase, but splits: 'to break' scrambles the urge, and 'into' places it within the edge letters of 'Kashmir' (its apostrophe-s ignored).
explanation.definitionFit: The Kruger is South Africa's best-known wildlife reserve, a national park named after Paul Kruger.

clue.text: Grain yield report

indicators.note: report signals a word spoken, so it is the sound that counts

parts.note: to yield is to cede, give up

explanation.surface: A farming headline: the latest harvest figures for cereals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yield' looks like crop output; it is CEDE, give way, which is said like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A grain is a single seed of a cereal plant such as wheat.

clue.text: Talk covers an about-turn by the head of ecumenical religious office

indicators.note: covers says the talk word wraps round the reversed an

parts.note: to rabbit is British slang for to talk at length

indicators.note: an about-turn sends the word an backwards
the head of picks the first letter of ecumenical

explanation.surface: A church conversation where someone changes position under an ecumenical leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Talk' as a verb is British slang: to rabbit on is to chatter. 'about-turn' reverses 'an', which 'covers' tucks inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The rabbinate is the position or term held by a rabbi, a Jewish religious post.

clue.text: What's in author's envelope is fatal, if swallowed by an old lady

definitions.text: fatal, if swallowed by an old lady

indicators.note: what's in says the letters sit inside the run of words author's envelope

explanation.surface: A warning label: the contents of a writer's envelope are poisonous if eaten by an elderly woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition refers to the nursery rhyme 'There Was an Old Lady Who Swallowed a Fly', which ends with her swallowing a horse: 'she's dead, of course'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the rhyme the final animal the old woman gulps down kills her, so it is the fatal thing.

clue.text: Leaves with story about making Cornish pasty

indicators.note: about signals the letters of Cornish pasty being rearranged, once the letters of story are accounted for

explanation.surface: A cookery note: greens plus a tale about baking a pasty from Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: Composite: the answer and STORY together use the letters of CORNISH PASTY, rearranged ('about'). A Cornish pasty is a British baked pastry of meat and vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinach is a leafy vegetable eaten for its dark green foliage, so leaves fits loosely.

clue.text: I am shocked with young and old extremists joining resistance unit

indicators.note: joining says the end letters attach to the resistance unit

parts.note: the ohm is the unit of electrical resistance

indicators.note: extremists takes the end letters of young and of old

explanation.surface: Shock at youthful and elderly radicals signing up to a resistance movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resistance unit' suggests a guerrilla cell; it is the electrical unit. 'extremists' takes the ends of 'young' and 'old'.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is what someone blurts when startled, so it expresses being shocked.

clue.text: Slim figure at last is yours!

parts.note: slim and thin both mean slender

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of figure

explanation.surface: A dieting advert: the slender shape you want is finally yours.
explanation.definitionFit: Thine is the archaic possessive meaning belonging to you, an old form of yours.

clue.text: High level of the gender problem

indicators.note: a problem jumbles things, here the letters of the gender

explanation.surface: A comment on how severe the gender issue has become.
explanation.walkthrough: 'problem' rearranges THE GENDER.
explanation.definitionFit: To the utmost extent, or as far as possible, is the idiomatic meaning of the phrase.

clue.text: Something from Tchaikovsky for Brazil?

definitions.meaning: a tool for opening a Brazil, the large nut, not the country

explanation.surface: A quiz question about a Russian composer's piece for a South American country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brazil' looks like the country; it is the Brazil nut.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the famous ballet score; the other a hinged tool used to split hard shells.

clue.text: Rising affluence meant 'China era' not as planned

indicators.note: not as planned implies things went awry, so the remaining letters are jumbled
not says those letters are left out of the phrase

parts.note: as read as the plural of the letter a, so every A is meant

explanation.surface: An economics note: China's boom period did not unfold as intended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not as' removes the three As from MEANT CHINA ERA; 'planned', with 'not', rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Growing wealth is the process of making richer, so the noun suits increasing prosperity.

clue.text: Open marriage initially helped to clean out film-maker

indicators.note: out signals the letters being knocked out of order
initially takes the first letters of helped, to and clean

explanation.surface: A tabloid scenario: an open marriage helped a director clean up his act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives HTC from 'helped to clean'; 'out' rearranges them with OPEN MARRIAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: The director of photography is the person in charge of the camera work on a movie.

clue.text: Colonial address back in Nairobi has memories

indicators.note: back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A nostalgic line about Kenya's capital holding memories of the colonial era.
explanation.walkthrough: The run 'Nairobi has memories' holds the answer backwards. MEMSAHIB was how Indians addressed a European married woman under the Raj.
explanation.definitionFit: It was a form of respectful address used to European ladies in colonial India.

clue.text: One theologian upset over love for cheese

indicators.note: over says the overturned pair goes round love
upset says one and the theologian are turned upside down, read backwards in a down entry

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
a mullah is a Muslim scholar of religious law
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A religious scholar is distressed about a romance and turns to cheese for comfort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns I MULLAH into HALLUMI, and 'over' puts it round O to give HALL-O-UMI.
explanation.definitionFit: Halloumi is a firm salty Cypriot variety, often grilled, made from goat and sheep milk.

clue.text: Talked about less healthy lands covered in heather, bracken and trees

indicators.note: talked about signals that what counts is the spoken sound

parts.words: less healthy lands covered in heather, bracken
parts.note: less healthy is sicker, and upland areas covered with heather and bracken are moors

explanation.surface: Gossip about blighted upland vegetation and the trees growing there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Talked about' makes SICKER MOORS sound like the answer. Moors are open upland areas typical of northern Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The sycamore is a large maple-like tree common across Britain and Europe.

clue.text: Copper and cook disrupted interloper

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: disrupted says the letters of cook are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A police officer and a chef interrupted by an uninvited guest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' reads as a policeman but gives CU; 'disrupted' turns COOK into CKOO.
explanation.definitionFit: The cuckoo lays its eggs in other birds' nests, so it is a byword for an intruder.

clue.text: Stomach upset oddly not seen in school disco

indicators.note: oddly not seen says the odd-placed letters of school disco are dropped, keeping the even ones

explanation.surface: A child's tummy ache goes unnoticed at a school dance.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the 1st, 3rd, 5th... letters of 'school disco' to leave the even ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Colic is severe abdominal pain, especially in babies, so it is a bellyache.

clue.text: Curved kind of oven found in empty chateaux

indicators.note: found in says the rearranged oven sits within the outer letters
empty strips out the middle of chateaux leaving its first and last letters
kind of hints at a variant form of oven, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A curved type of cooker discovered in abandoned French castles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kind of' rearranges OVEN as ONVE; 'empty' leaves CX from 'chateaux'. 'kind of oven' also hints at a convection oven.
explanation.definitionFit: A convex surface bulges outward, so it is curved like the outside of a sphere.

clue.text: Old broken chair engulfed by current

indicators.note: engulfed by puts the broken chair inside the current

parts.note: AC is alternating current

indicators.note: broken says the letters of chair are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: An antique, broken chair swept away by a river current.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' looks like a river's flow; it is electrical alternating current, which 'engulfed by' wraps round the scrambled chair.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic means belonging to a much earlier period, antiquated.

clue.text: Help N-Z?

parts.note: N to Z is the second half of the alphabet, and the second half of the letters of the word alphabet reads a, b, e, t

explanation.surface: A cry for assistance, perhaps from New Zealand.
explanation.walkthrough: N-Z looks like New Zealand; it is the back half of the alphabet, so take the back half of the word ALPHABET.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to assist or encourage, usually in wrongdoing.

clue.text: Brush round a French officers' mess once

indicators.note: round says the brush word goes around the French article

parts.note: to groom a horse is to brush it
un is French for a

explanation.surface: Tidying up an old French military dining room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a French' is the French word for a, not a French person. 'once' marks the definition as historical: a warship's junior officers' mess.
explanation.definitionFit: On old warships the gunroom was where junior officers ate, hence a historical mess.

clue.text: Delight at the start of 'Gimme Shelter'

indicators.note: at the start of takes the opening letter of Gimme

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind

explanation.surface: Joy at the opening bars of the Rolling Stones song 'Gimme Shelter'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gimme Shelter' reads as a song title; split it into G and LEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Glee is great joy or merriment, the same feeling as delight.

clue.text: What may be found in the gut in ulcerative colitis

definitions.text: What may be found in the gut

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the run ulcerative colitis

explanation.surface: A medical question about what appears in an inflamed bowel condition.
explanation.definitionFit: The bacterium Escherichia coli lives naturally in human intestines, so it is a gut microbe.

clue.text: Jury may be missing one side

definitions.meaning: a jury has twelve members, so with one absent it has this many
a football or cricket team fields this many players

explanation.surface: A court remark that a juror is absent, leaving a team short.
explanation.definitionFit: Twelve jurors less one gives the number in a soccer or cricket team, which Britons call a side.
